findings.explanation: Splunkbase app 4856 is the community 'Metrics Add-on for Infrastructure' (TA-linux-metrics), not an NSX add-on; no Splunk-supported `Splunk_TA_vmware-nsxt` exists. The NSX options on Splunkbase are the VMware-built 'VMware NSX-T Splunk App' (4241) and the community 'VMware NSX add-on' TA-nsx (6805). The same wrong ID repeats in dataSources, detailedImplementation and references.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with the real NSX integration (e.g. VMware NSX-T Splunk App, Splunkbase 4241, and/or TA-nsx, Splunkbase 6805) or describe the feed as custom syslog/REST ingestion; then re-derive sourcetype names from whichever add-on is chosen.

findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1810 is 'Hunk App for MongoDB'. The Splunk Add-on for VMware (splunk_TA_vmware) is Splunkbase 3215. Repeated in dataSources, detailedImplementation and references.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Splunk Add-on for VMware, Splunkbase 3215 (https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/3215).

findings.explanation: The Splunk Add-on for VMware has no `vmware:vmware:vsphere:vcenter` sourcetype; VM inventory (guest IPs, names) is `vmware:inv:vm` and vCenter logs are `vmware:vclog:*`. The same invented sourcetype appears in app and detailedImplementation.

Since the named add-on does not exist, these sourcetype names cannot come from it; the VMware NSX-T Splunk App (4241) and TA-nsx (6805) use their own sourcetypes. The text also says the REST JSON is ingested 'through' the TA, but the implementation section says custom HTTPS collectors are needed.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the sourcetypes defined by Splunkbase 4241/6805 props.conf; state clearly that dfw_groups/dfw_policy are site-defined sourcetypes produced by a custom Policy API collector.

findings.explanation: detailedImplementation alert design uses a 15-minute window, but the SPL bins `span=1h` over -24h, so `flow_events` is an hourly count and cannot be compared to a 15m threshold; the 7-day 3σ baseline also has no counterpart in the 24h search.
findings.suggested_fix: Either state thresholds per 1h bin consistent with the SPL, or document a separate 15m alert search and a separate 7-day baseline search.

findings.explanation: The implementation, dataSources and title promise Applied-To scope and policy-coverage analysis from `vmware:nsxt:dfw_policy`, but the SPL only reads firewall/IDFW verdict lines and an IP→group lookup; `applied_to`, `sequence_number` and policy JSON are never searched. Readers will expect shadowed-rule and scope-drift output the search does not produce.
findings.quote: maintain Splunk lookups expanding **NSGroup** membership per IP; run the **`spl`** saved search hourly
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the detection as flow-vs-NSGroup coverage classification, and move applied-to / policy-scope review to a separate documented search (or a sibling UC such as UC-18.2.7).

findings.explanation: Traceflow in NSX Manager lives under Plan & Troubleshoot > Traceflow; 'Plan Tier-1' is not a UI path.
NSX Policy DFW categories are Ethernet, Emergency, Infrastructure, Environment and Application; 'Default' is a default policy inside Application, not a category value.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm against the NSX 4.2 Policy API SecurityPolicy.category enum and list the actual values.

findings.explanation: An SNMP UPS model has nothing to do with NSX DFW enforcement posture.
The UC is marked verified by an automated agent while carrying wrong Splunkbase IDs and an invented sourcetype; there is no evidence of SME sign-off.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft/community until a human SME validates against a live NSX feed.

findings.explanation: The search does not check which workloads policies are applied to; it classifies observed flows by whether source/destination IPs fall in known groups.
findings.quote: that firewall blueprints still wrap the workloads they should
findings.suggested_fix: Say it looks at real traffic and flags connections allowed to or from machines that are not in any security group, or allowed between different groups.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: NSX DFW packet logs report the permit action as PASS (actions PASS, DROP, REJECT) and identify the rule as `<ruleset>/<rule-id>`. `verdict_norm` only maps ALLOW/ACCEPT, and both `_raw` fallbacks look for ALLOW (`\bALLOW\b`, `INET match (ALLOW|DROP|REJECT)`), so permitted flows never become ALLOW and the `unmapped_source_on_permit`, `allow_toward_peer_outside_nsgroups` and `cross_nsg_allow_needs_review` classes cannot fire on native logs. Add PASS to the ALLOW mapping and parse rule IDs from the `ruleset/id` token rather than assuming a `seq|policy|rule` RULE_TAG tuple.
Title promises 'Applied-To Scope, and Policy Coverage Gaps' but the SPL never reads policy/applied_to data; it only classifies flows by IP→NSGroup lookup.

Branch `unmapped_source_on_permit` fires on `verdict_norm IN ("ALLOW","REJECT")`; REJECT is not a permit, so the label and logic disagree. Also the `_raw` fallback `\bALLOW\b`/`\bDROP\b` can match rule names or other text, and a CSV lookup may return multivalue groups for IPs in several NSGroups, making `src_group_path!=dst_group_path` comparisons unreliable.

summary: The SPL and search-logic notes describe a coherent flow-to-NSGroup lookup detection, but NSX logs permits as PASS (which the SPL never maps to ALLOW), the add-on identity is wrong throughout (Splunkbase 4856 and 1810 are unrelated apps, `Splunk_TA_vmware` sourcetype is invented), the title/implementation promise applied-to and policy-coverage analysis the SPL never performs, and the alert thresholds do not match the search grain.
